source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Check AST1060 is provision
2. Destroy the BIOS active region
3. Use DediProg to program BIOS firmware with bad-active region into the BIOS SPI flash
4. Boot the BIOS and AST1060 will recover BIOS firmware

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: 1. AST1060 checks BIOS verify ok and BIOS boot up success

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: Operator stages forced-bad BIOS recovery; agent only reads BMC controller information after recovery.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: Recovery flow and post-recovery BIOS version.
deepseek_columns.risk: Deliberately breaks firmware; never power-cut mid-recovery.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL; recognizes deliberate corruption and operator staging but its BMC `mc info` probe cannot prove BIOS recovery.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED; adds exact SPI/AST1060/image/DediProg settings, stable power, console/OOB, rollback and post-boot evidence.
historical_reviews.round_02: No separate exact-code round-02 entry was found.
historical_reviews.second_review_handoff: Confirms DediProg hardware setup and firmware destruction remain operator-controlled while recovery evidence can be collected systematically.

original_test_intent: Prove that the provisioned AST1060 can detect and recover a deliberately invalid BIOS active region programmed into the exact SPI device, restore a verified BIOS image and return the platform to successful boot.
original_method: A qualified hardware operator connects and verifies the DediProg fixture on the powered-safe exact SPI target, programs the owner-approved bad-active image with full verify evidence, disconnects/restores the fixture state as required, then boots while automation records AST1060 recovery, BIOS verification, POST, target identity and system health.
manual_activity: A qualified operator must physically identify and connect the DediProg programmer/adapter to the correct BIOS SPI device, set voltage/write protection and place the board in the documented programming state. After that setup and approval, the exact program/verify transaction and AST1060 recovery/boot evidence can be automated.
required_inputs: Exact board revision, BIOS SPI part/topology, active-region map and AST1060 provisioning state
Approved bad-active fixture, known-good recovery image, hashes and construction specification
DediProg model/software/version, adapter/pinout, voltage, power-state, write-protect and exact program/verify syntax
Qualified operator, ESD controls, stable power, maintenance authorization and KVM/serial/OOB
AST1060 recovery trigger, timeout, expected target BIOS and validated manual fallback/rollback
safety_requirements: Positively identify SPI target, pin 1, voltage, isolation and board power state before attaching or enabling the programmer.
Program only the approved bad-active fixture and verify every byte; do not corrupt an unspecified region or production system.
Do not interrupt power during AST1060 recovery; stop on wrong target, programmer verify failure, recovery timeout, OOB loss or critical power/thermal anomaly.
Preserve the first failure and programmer/console evidence; do not auto-retry programming, boot or recovery.
agent_execution_scope: Validate target/image/programmer/recovery manifest and capture pre-test BIOS/AST1060/BMC/SEL/POST baseline.
After operator fixture attestation and approval, run the exact supported program-and-verify transaction if remotely controllable, then monitor the single recovery boot through KVM/serial/OOB.
Collect restored BIOS identity, AST1060 verification, POST/boot and health evidence and report Tool Result without setting PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve deliberate BIOS-region corruption and the exact target/images/recovery boundary.
Perform and attest physical DediProg connection, board power/isolation and any required manual fixture removal.
Supervise fallback recovery and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its post-recovery `ipmitool mc info` reads BMC identity, not BIOS version, AST1060 recovery or boot success. It is at most supplemental and cannot establish the criterion.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the validated DediProg software/CLI for exact SPI program and byte verification only after operator fixture attestation, then capture AST1060 recovery and BIOS/POST evidence through approved console/OOB interfaces.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: AST1060 provisioning, active-region destruction, DediProg SPI programming, recovery boot and 60/60-minute fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.status: AUTOMATED PROGRAM/RECOVERY EVIDENCE AFTER MANUAL FIXTURE SETUP
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind the DediProg transaction to a signed target/region/image manifest, require operator photo/continuity/power attestation, preserve program-and-verify output, and record AST1060 recovery milestones plus restored BIOS/POST health.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only the exact board/SPI/AST1060/DediProg fixture combination.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record board, SPI, AST1060, BIOS/BMC, DediProg software and image versions/hashes.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform SPI/AST1060 recovery documentation and DediProg hardware/software instructions must be supplied.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds target-safe fixture attestation and complete recovery evidence without replacing deliberate bad-active programming.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; destructive stimulus, AST1060 recovery verification and successful boot remain required.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Complete hardware fixture and recovery manifest.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Incorrect clip orientation, voltage, isolation or target can permanently damage hardware; software cannot attest the physical hookup by itself.

project_override_considerations: A project may define its own board-specific bad-active fixture and recovery image, but may not replace DediProg corruption with a normal capsule failure and claim equivalent recovery coverage.
expected_evidence: Board/SPI/AST1060/BIOS identity, region map, image hashes, DediProg settings and authorization
Operator-attributed fixture/power/ESD/write-protect attestation and pre-test baseline
Complete erase/program/verify transcript for the approved bad-active image
AST1060 recovery trigger/timing/verify, restored target BIOS, POST/boot/KVM/BMC/SEL health, Tool Result and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and criterion consistently require deliberate bad-active SPI programming followed by AST1060 recovery and successful boot.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The destructive operation and recovery acceptance are clear. Missing fixture/images/settings are readiness inputs; the manual physical hookup followed by automatable programming/recovery core fits REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retains PARTIAL boundary but rejects BMC controller info as sufficient proof.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on package/user-confirmation classification and retains its exact physical fixture, recovery and boot gates.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates operator fixture attestation from executable program/recovery stages and requires byte-level and recovery-milestone evidence.

review_improvement: Provides a safe boundary for physical SPI programming and prevents a BMC identity read from being misreported as BIOS recovery proof.
independent_technical_reasoning: The source explicitly requires an external DediProg connection and hardware programming setup, so the case is not fully automatable. Once a qualified operator completes that physical setup, the program/verify transaction and recovery/boot monitoring can be automated, making PARTIAL—not MANUAL ONLY or BLOCKED—the correct capability.
